However, due to its well-documented multisystem toxicity, it has no direct clinical therapeutic value. Therefore, bisphenol A should be considered solely as a structural probe for mechanistic studies rather than a therapeutic candidate. This study identified UQCRC1, PRDX4, and PDK2 as candidate biomarkers for keloids (KD), providing theoretical support for elucidating the regulatory mechanisms of mitochondria and programmed cell death in keloids. All conclusions were based solely on bioinformatic analyses without in vitro or in vivo experimental validation, thus the findings remain hypothetical and require rigorous confirmation in future studies.

articles.title: Epidemiology and prognostic factors in older adults with severe burns (≥10% TBSA): A 13-year retrospective study from a French national burn center.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: High mortality in older burn patients results from the combination of acute injury and physiological decline. While total body surface area burned (TBSA) and age are established prognostic factors, the interplay between acute metabolic derangement and chronic comorbidity burden remains poorly characterized. This study evaluated the prognostic value of the lactate/albumin Ratio (LAR) and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Secondary endpoints included identifying independent mortality predictors and establishing the lethal area 50 percent (LA50) thresholds. A retrospective study at a National Burn Center (location blinded) included all patients aged > 65 years with burns > 10% TBSA (2012-2025). The LAR assessed the coupling of tissue hypoxia and nutritional status. Chronic disease burden was quantified using the weighted CCI. Multivariate logistic regression identified risk factors for in-hospital mortality. Among 243 patients (mean age 75.8 years, TBSA 26.9%), mortality was 35.0%. In the complete-case analysis for biomarkers (n = 178), LAR discrimination was strong (AUC=0.84), comparable to lactate alone (mmol/L) (AUC=0.81, p = 0.09), but significantly superior to albumin (g/dL) (AUC=0.74, p = 0.014). A cut-off of LAR > 1.0 was identified as a critical threshold for mortality. In multivariate analysis, while binary comorbidities showed no significance, the CCI emerged as a robust independent predictor (OR 1.71, p < 0.001). Other independent predictors included TBSA, inhalation injury, and the LAR (OR 2.15, p = 0.006). The LA50 threshold was established at 34% TBSA. Mortality in older adults can be interpreted through a conceptual "double hit" model: acute metabolic shock (LAR) and chronic comorbidities (CCI). The LAR offers comparable predictive value to isolated markers while integrating nutritional status, suggesting an exploratory and cohort-specific "LAR Unity Threshold" for risk stratification.

articles.title: How the world manages acute burns: Insights from an international survey of 106 burn units across 50 countries.
authors: National Burn Care, Education & Research group the Netherlands
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: There is considerable variability in the management of acute burns globally, including differences between low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and high-income countries (HICs). This study aimed to describe global surgical burn care practices through an international survey, providing insight into diagnostic, debridement, and coverage techniques and their timing. An online survey was developed and distributed to burn surgeons worldwide, focusing on the management of four patient cases and standard practices. The survey was developed and tested in collaboration with burn care experts, and distributed via email. One respondent per hospital performing burn surgery was permitted to prevent duplication. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Fisher's exact tests and Chi-square tests, with responses categorised by country and regional economic status. Burn surgeons from 106 burn units across 50 countries completed the survey, achieving a 44% response rate. Early surgical debridement (<48 h) was most commonly referred to as standard care, although definitions of early grafting differed. LMICs and HICs differed in the availability of diagnostic tools, enzymatic debridement, and wound coverage techniques. Further regional differences were observed among HICs in Europe, North America, and Oceania, highlighting diverse approaches to burn care worldwide. This study offers a global overview of acute surgical burn management, showing both universally common practices and significant regional variations between LMICs, HICs, and continents. The broad heterogeneity in surgical timing and techniques highlights the need for further research.

articles.title: Performance of Sepsis-3 criteria in burn patients: A multicenter real-world study.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among patients with burn injury, yet diagnosis is particularly challenging because burn-induced hypermetabolic and inflammatory responses frequently mimic infection-related organ dysfunction. Although multiple sepsis definitions are used in clinical practice, their diagnostic performance and prognostic relevance in real-world burn populations remain uncertain. We conducted a retrospective multicenter validation study using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network. Adult patients hospitalized with burn injury were identified. Clinically documented sepsis, defined by ICD-10-CM codes A40, A41, or R65.2 occurring within 7 days after the index burn event, served as the reference standard. The diagnostic accuracy of Sepsis-3, American Burn Association (ABA), and Mann-Salinas (MN) criteria was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Prognostic relevance was evaluated by comparing 28-day all-cause mortality across sepsis definitions using propensity score-matched cohorts and Cox proportional hazards models. Among 527,197 adult burn patients, 8810 (1.4%) had clinically documented sepsis. Sensitivity was high across definitions (ABA, 86.7%; Mann-Salinas, 86.6%; Sepsis-3, 81.4%), whereas specificity varied substantially (Mann-Salinas, 77.0%; ABA, 61.6%; Sepsis-3, 45.8%). PPVs were uniformly low (2.5%-6.0%), reflecting substantial overclassification in this low-prevalence population, while NPVs exceeded 99% for all criteria. No significant differences in 28-day mortality were observed between definitions, with all pairwise hazard ratios overlapping and crossing unity. In adult burn patients, commonly used sepsis definitions function primarily as sensitive screening tools rather than confirmatory diagnostic instruments. The Mann-Salinas criteria demonstrated the most balanced performance. Sepsis assessment in burn populations should integrate physiologic criteria, clinical judgment, and confirmatory infection testing.

articles.title: Improving Naloxone and Buprenorphine Provision in the Pediatric Emergency Department Through Education and Chief Complaint-Triggered Screening.
articles.abstract: Opioid use disorder (OUD) among US adolescents represents a public health crisis, with overdose deaths becoming a leading cause of mortality. Despite their efficacy, naloxone and buprenorphine remain underutilized. The pediatric emergency department (PED) presents an intervention opportunity, as many adolescents with OUD present there before fatal overdoses. This quality improvement initiative examined the use of education and hybrid screening to improve the provision of naloxone and buprenorphine in the PED. A multifaceted OUD screening and treatment protocol was implemented in a PED using Best Practice Alerts (BPA) triggered by specific chief complaints (CC), alerting providers to the need for additional screening. Components included provider education, formulary changes, and clinical pathways. Data from adolescent encounters over 45 months were analyzed, comparing naloxone and buprenorphine prescribing rates before and after implementation. Secondary analyses examined demographics, insurance, and psychiatric comorbidities. During the study, 63 adolescents initiated buprenorphine, and 246 received naloxone. Among patients with BPA-qualifying CCs, naloxone dispensing increased from 3.89% to 11.39% and buprenorphine prescribing increased from 1.04% to 2.46%. Postimplementation, Black/African American adolescents and those with government insurance received more medications than peers, and overall naloxone prescribing increased from 0.4% to 0.79% of all visits. Patients triggering the BPA experienced longer ED stays regardless of medication receipt, with no increase in return visits. Electronic screening alerts coupled with provider education increased the provision of medications for adolescents at risk for opioid-related harm. The intervention is achievable in a PED without increasing return visits.

articles.title: Comment on "Validation of the Intensive Care Infection Score for infection discrimination in burn patients compared with other inflammatory biomarkers (ICARUS study).".
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries

articles.title: A burning issue: Methamphetamine intoxication is associated with graft loss.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Methamphetamine intoxication can lead to medical complications in burn patients, including longer intensive care unit (ICU) stays, sepsis, and more burn debridement procedures. However, its impact on graft durability remains unexplored. We hypothesize that methamphetamine-positive burn patients have higher rates of graft loss. A single center retrospective cohort study of patients admitted to the burn service from 2021 to 2024 was performed at an American Burn Association (ABA)-verified burn center. Patients were age 18 years or over, had toxicology screening, and were excluded if not screened for methamphetamine. The primary outcome measured was graft loss requiring return to operating room for re-graft or flap repair. Patient demographics, burn etiology, and use of autograft, along with ICU days, ventilator days, and length of stay were recorded. 746 patients were included in this study with median age 48 years and median total burn surface area burned for the full cohort of 8.35%. 112 patients were methamphetamine-positive. Methamphetamine users had higher rates of autograft loss (p < 0.001), even on logistic regression analysis. Methamphetamine users had increased TBSA (p = 0.01), longer hospital stays (p = 0.03), and increased likelihood of undergoing endotracheal intubation (p = 0.01). Methamphetamine-positive patients presented primarily with flame burns (p < 0.001), while non-users presented primarily with scald burns (p < 0.001). Methamphetamine-positive burn patients were more likely to sustain flame burns, undergo autografting, and experience graft loss as a complication. Methamphetamine is a unique risk factor for burn patients that increases risk of failing graft management. Routine toxicology testing can promptly identify these patients and notify providers earlier to plan for more intensive burn management.

articles.title: "It's calm on the outside but going absolutely stir crazy on the inside": A qualitative insight into the emotional dimensions and support for parent-administered at home paediatric burn dressing changes.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Globally, paediatric burns are the fifth most common non-fatal injury in children. In England and Wales annually over 30,000 children receive outpatient burn treatment. A paediatric burn can have a significant negative psychological impact on parents and children. In the UK, where parents are often asked to undertake their child's burn wound dressing changes at home, the role of clinical caregiver can provoke significant emotional labour. This study explored the emotional dimensions and support available to parents administering children's burn dressing changes at home. This qualitative study formed part of a larger experience-based co-design project to develop service guidance to support parent-administered home dressing changes in paediatric burns care. Clinic observations were conducted across three paediatric burns centres in England and Wales. In addition, semi-structured interviews were conducted with healthcare professionals and parents on the perspectives and experiences of parent-administered home dressing changes. A thematic framework analysis identified two key themes and sub-themes. Healthcare professionals typically recognised parental anxiety and regularly provided parents with comfort and reassurance in clinics. Healthcare professional perceptions of severity of anxiety displayed through parents' behaviour were used as indicators of suitability for home administered dressing changes. Whilst parents dealt with the practical elements of dressing changes, they were unprepared for the emotional impact. Parents expressed feeling negative emotions when administering dressing changes and employing strategies to supress emotions to minimise distress to their child. The emotional impact of paediatric burns is recognised by parents and healthcare professionals. However, a disparity exists between these perspectives. Currently guidance and reassurance provided to parents does not address the emotional impact of parent-administered dressing-changes. Healthcare professionals provide emotional support in clinic and task-related support for home dressing-changes. Resources to support parents to administer dressings at home should include psychological coping strategies to manage the negative impact on families.

articles.title: Projecting the incidence of burn injuries and its associated economic burden for 195 countries.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Burn injuries remain a persistent global health burden affecting low- and middle-income countries. Projections of future incidence and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) are needed to guide prevention and resource allocation. Age-, sex-, and country-specific burn incidence and DALY rates were pulled from the Global Burden of Disease and combined with World Bank population projections for 2030, 2040, and 2050 to generate estimates by country and region. Economic burden was modeled by multiplying DALYs by gross domestic product (GDP) per capita. Globally, projected burn cases increase from 10,319,496 in 2030 to 10,865,524 in 2050 (+5%), while disability-adjusted life years rise from 11,517,819 to 14,144,178 (+18.6%). The burden is concentrated in South Asia, reaching 1,627,305 cases in 2050, and in Sub-Saharan Africa, which rises to 3,850,835 cases. Individuals aged 15-19 years account for the largest share of global cases in both 2030 and 2050. Among young adults and children under 19 years, India is projected to have the highest burden, with 334,168 cases in 2030. The global burden remains balanced between males and females, with women representing 52% of cases through 2050. Case-to-population ratios highlight disproportionate burdens in smaller nations, with Chad, Argentina, and Azerbaijan among the countries with the highest per-capita rates. In economic terms, the United States produces the largest cost estimate at $20.6 billion, while countries such as India ($13.2 B) and China ($14.5 B) carry substantial burdens driven by extremely high DALY counts despite moderate GDP per capita. Burn-related morbidity remains a significant global challenge, particularly in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, with children disproportionately affected. Investment in prevention and burn care is essential to reduce inequities.

articles.title: An improved classification of keloids based on morphology, topography, and heterogeneity for prognosis and treatment.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Keloids are benign tumors resulting from pathological scarring and excessive collagen deposition with diverse clinical presentations. The treatment of keloids remains challenging, often leading to recurrences. In this study, we propose an enhanced morphological classification, derived from both previous research and a retrospective analysis of 95 keloids treated surgically in our department with a global recurrence rate of 41.1% over an average follow-up of 3.75 years. We have analyzed the clinical presentation, together with prognosis and recommendations of treatment for the several keloid phenotypes we identified. This analysis enables us to propose a keloid classification defining 5 categories: type I - Acne keloïdalis nuchae (AKN); type II - Nodular outside the ear; type III - Nodular of the ear; type IV - Superficial spreading; type V - Mixed shape. This new clinical classification of keloids was statistically predictive for the risk of recurrence after surgery (p = 0.0158). Of interest, this proposed classification not only captured all keloid presentations but also provided valuable insights for prognosis and treatment. Type I showed a favorable prognosis, with less than 20% recurrence after extralesional excision and wound healing. Types II, III, and IV had moderate recurrence rates (30-50%). Nodular keloids were treated with intralesional excision and suture, followed by corticosteroid injections. Type V, however, had a poor prognosis with a 75% recurrence rate post-surgery. This phenotype-based classification offers a better understanding of keloid pathophysiology and optimization of treatment strategies tailored to specific keloid types.

articles.title: HMGB1 release initiates burn wound healing delay via HMGB1-produced DNA gap reduction, promoting DNA damage-hypomethylation-senescence cascade.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Burn wound healing is delayed due to a reduction in the epigenetic DNA protection marker, which promotes senescence. In the rat burn model, high mobility group box protein 1 (HMGB1)-produced DNA gap reduction induces DNA damage and impairs the wound-healing process. Overexpression of Box A, an HMGB1 domain, enhances DNA stability and promotes second-degree burn wound healing through the molecular process of DNA gap formation. However, the mechanisms responsible for HMGB1-produced DNA gap reduction in burn wounds remain unknown. In the cell culture model, we found that high temperatures stimulated the release of HMGB1 protein from the nucleus, resulting in a long-term decrease in DNA gaps. This reduction caused increased DNA damage, Alu hypomethylation, and eventual senescence, potentially limiting cutaneous wound healing processes. To reproduce DNA gaps, we applied exogenous Box A to transfect into burn wounds. In comparison to the other groups subjected to the same conditions, including no plasmid-treated group and plasmid control-treated group, the Alu methylation levels were significantly increased in the Box A-treated group. Meanwhile, a DNA damage marker (γH2A.X) and DNA damage response (DDR) signals (p53, p21, and p16) were all significantly decreased. As a result, reduced senescent cells and promoted cell proliferation, as well as accelerated wound confluence, all of which considerably improved wound healing in the group that received Box A treatment. Our findings revealed that HMGB1 release functions as an upstream mechanism in the molecular pathogenesis of burns, and Box A gene therapy could provide a targeted therapeutic strategy in burn wound treatment.

articles.title: Mechanism of ferroptosis in progressive injury of skeletal muscle caused by high-voltage electrical burns and the intervention effect of uAMC3203.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: The mechanism underlying progressive skeletal muscle injury following high-voltage electrical burns (HVEB) remains unclear. Therefore, clarifying this mechanism is essential for developing targeted treatment. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between the healthy rats and those with severe muscle contusion were identified using the GSE162565 dataset. Differentially expressed ferroptosis-related genes (DE-FRGs) were extracted, and core genes were screened through bioinformatics analyses. A rat model of HVEB-induced skeletal muscle injury was established, including solvent and ferroptosis-inhibitor (uAMC3202) intervention groups. Skeletal muscle tissues were analyzed for biochemical, functional, histological, transcriptional, and protein-level modifications. In the severe skeletal muscle contusion model, DEGs at each time point were enriched in the ferroptosis pathway, and five core genes were identified. Macroscopic wound evaluation, functional exercise assessment, histological analysis, and serum creatine kinase measurements confirmed that HVEB induced progressive skeletal muscle damage. At selected post-injury time points, the HVEB group exhibited significantly higher expression levels of Hmox1, Timp1, and Hif1a than those in the control group. Additionally, the expression levels of proteins associated with iron and lipid metabolism increased at specific time points after HVEB. Administration of the ferroptosis inhibitor uAMC3203, markedly attenuated the elevated expressions of Hmox1 and iron metabolism-related proteins in the HVEB injury group at one week. In a rat model of HVEB-induced skeletal muscle injury, Hmox1, Timp1, and Hif1a were upregulated during injury progression. Moreover, uAMC3203 mitigated Hmox1 overexpression and iron metabolism activation in damaged skeletal muscles during the first week following HVEB.

articles.title: Causes of inappropriate hospitalization and direct financial burden: Evidence from an Iranian burns hospital.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Inappropriate hospitalization is a significant issue that imposes medical and financial pressure on hospitals, patients, and payers. By addressing this issue, healthcare costs can be minimized, while maintaining the quality of services. This study aimed to identify factors causing inappropriate hospitalization of burns patients and to calculate the financial burden associated with it in a hospital in Iran. This is mixed methods study conducted during 2024-2025. The quantitative phase focused on the medical records of hospitalized patients, from which 342 cases were selected. The medical records were evaluated based on the Appropriateness Evaluation Protocol. To investigate the causes of inappropriate hospitalization, a semi-structured interview was conducted with 11 senior and middle managers. Qualitative content analysis was used for data analysis. About 24% of patients experienced at least one day of inappropriate stay, with approximately 4.5% of the total hospitalization days deemed inappropriate. Marital status, insurance status, and length of stay were significantly associated with the rate of inappropriate hospitalization (p < 0.05). The estimated annual number of inappropriate hospitalization days per patient was 1057 days, and the direct cost incurred by patients was 14,309,430,289 Rials ($24,902). The primary causes of inappropriate hospitalizations were attributed to care providers, service recipients, financial issues, and extra-organizational factors. A significant percentage of burns patients experience unnecessary hospitalizations, leading to significant direct costs. Hospitals can further minimize unnecessary stays and reduce hospital costs by properly managing bed occupancy, monitoring medical staff and patients, and educating both groups.

articles.title: Expanded burn registry: Epidemiological profile, clinical variables, and multivariate analysis of outcomes in the Dominican Republic (2020-2024).
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Burns represent a significant global public health problem, imposing a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. In the Dominican Republic, a previous study in the pediatric population revealed a concerning profile of high mortality and frequent electrical burns, raising critical questions for adults. To describe the epidemiological profile, identify independent predictors of mortality, and benchmark outcomes against international severity metrics in adult burn patients in the Dominican Republic. This retrospective cohort study included 1005 adult patients (≥15 years) admitted to the country's main burn reference center (2020-2024). Demographic, clinical, and event-related variables were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression, probit analysis for LA50, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves were used. Overall mortality was 32.2%. The cohort was predominantly male (73.4%), with a median age of 37 years. Men sustained mainly electrical burns (37.7%) in occupational settings (48.5%); women, flame burns (64.0%) in the domestic sphere (74.9%). Independent mortality predictors were TBSA ≥ 60% (aOR 29.85, 95% CI 11.37-78.34), complications (aOR 250.00, 95% CI 55.56-1000.00), full-thickness depth (aOR 4.33, 95% CI 2.48-7.58), and inhalation injury (aOR 2.09, 95% CI 0.98-4.46). The LA50 was 48.0% (95% CI 45.0-50.9%). Median survival was 42.0 days, decreasing to 4.0 days for TBSA ≥ 60% and 20.0 days for septic patients (log-rank p < 0.001 and p = 0.012). The leading causes of death were septic shock (40.1%) and respiratory failure (36.1%). This registry reveals one of the highest global burn mortality rates, driven by extensive injuries and complications. The LA50 of 48.0% and the predominance of sepsis-related deaths underscore the extreme vulnerability of this population and the urgent need for targeted prevention, strengthened clinical protocols, and a prospective national registry to guide interventions and reduce mortality.

articles.title: Burning questions: ED management of pediatric burns at a non-burn health care system.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: American Burn Association (ABA) referral criteria help identify patients to be transferred. Limited data exist on characteristics of patients being transferred and utilization of these criteria at non-burn centers (NBC). To describe pediatric emergency department (ED) disposition practices at a non-burn center and compare these practices to ABA referral criteria. Retrospective review of electronic records of patients < 18 years old, with discharge diagnosis of burn at a non-burn healthcare system, from December 2016 to June 2022, was performed. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze transfer rates and determine odds ratios of different factors, comparing transferred and discharged patients. 1231 cases were identified with 35% transferred. Of the 65% of patients discharged, 52% met ABA referral criteria. For all visits, 64% met at least one ABA criterion, of which 47% were transferred. Infants had greatest odds of transfer (OR 9.62, 95% CI 4.6 - 20.1). Burns to high-risk anatomical zones (OR 5.89, 95% CI 4.1 - 8.4), those with > 20% total body surface area (OR 16.86, 95% CI 4.3 - 66.7) and full/partial thickness burns (OR 11.47, 95% CI 5.5 - 23.9) were also all associated with highest odds of transfer. The majority of visits met ABA criteria for transfer to a burn center; however, only about half those qualified were transferred. Some may have been appropriately discharged. Infants, large burns, burns to high-risk anatomic zones, or full/partial thickness burns were more often transferred indicating appropriate adherence to the established guideline. These data suggest that ABA criteria are very broad for pediatrics and do not have face validity for community physicians. Further work is needed to refine pediatric ABA referral criteria.

articles.title: Transportation mode impact on care service utilization and community integration after burn injury - A Burn Model System National Database Study.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Community health is affected by transportation access, an underexplored factor in burn outcomes. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the associations of transportation mode with health service utilization and social community integration after burn injury. A multicenter burn longitudinal dataset was analyzed from 2018 to 2024. Self-reported transportation modality was examined primarily six months post-injury. The population was categorized into two groups: driving their own vehicle (DOV) and other modes of transportation (OMT). Outcomes included community integration and four health services (physical/occupational therapy, peer support, psychological services, and burn-related surgeries). Regression analyses examined the association between transportation mode and health services, and community integration, controlling for demographic and clinical factors. Of the 563 participants, 373 (66.3%) reported DOV, 151 (26.8%) riding with someone else, and 31 (5.5%) using public transit. The regression model demonstrated that the DOV group had higher community integration than the OMT group (b = 1.23; 95% CI = 0.74, 1.71; p < 0.001). Logistic regression analyses revealed no significant associations between DOV and service utilization, controlling for demographic and clinical variables. DOV was associated with better social integration. Addressing transportation barriers may contribute to improved social integration outcomes after burn injury.

articles.title: Validation and reliability of three functional tests in hospitalized burned subjects.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: To study the validity, reliability, standard error of the mean (SEM), minimum detectable change (MDC95), and learning effect of three functional capacity tests in hospitalized burn victims: 5-repetition Sit-to-Stand (STS_5r), 1-minute Sit-to-Stand (STS_1min) and Timed up-and-go (TUG). In a cross-sectional study, 64 subjects were evaluated. The tests were randomly applied by two evaluators in three assessment moments: twice by the same evaluator (intra-rater) with a 1-day interval; and once by a second evaluator after the first assessment (inter-rater). 6-minute walk test (6MWT) and assessment of quadriceps femoris (QF) muscle strength were also performed. For analysis of the learning effect, all tests were repeated two times at each assessment moment. The TUG showed very strong correlation with the 6MWT (r = -0.90, p < 0.0001), whereas for the STS_5r and STS_1min the correlation was moderate (r = -0.55 and 0.60, respectively; p < 0.0001). As for the QF muscle strength test, there was moderate correlation with the TUG (r = -0.41, p = 0.0008) and rather modest correlations with the STS_5r (r = -0.30, p = 0.013) and the STS_1min (r = 0.21, p = 0.091). Intraclass correlation coefficient values were good to excellent in all intra- and inter-rater tests (0.88-0.97). MDC95 values ranged from 19% to 23%. Moreover, a small but statistically significant learning effect was observed in all tests. The STS_5r, STS_1min and TUG tests are valid and reliable to assess functional capacity of hospitalized burn victims, despite a small learning effect indicating the need to perform two tests. SEM and MDC values here described can be used in clinical practice to improve interpretability of the tests' results.

articles.title: Persistent immune dysregulation consistent with chronic low-grade inflammation in paediatric burn survivors.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: To characterise long-term immune dysregulation and persistent inflammatory signalling in paediatric burn survivors with hypertrophic scarring. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma were analysed from 20 paediatric participants: 10 burn survivors with hypertrophic scarring (median 4.1 years post-injury) and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Multiparameter flow cytometry, multiplex cytokine analysis, and quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were used to assess immune cell phenotypes, inflammatory mediators, and inflammatory gene expression. Overall proportions of major immune cell subsets were comparable between groups. However, burn survivors with hypertrophic scarring demonstrated increased CD4⁺TNFα⁺ cells, Th17 cells, CCR6⁺ natural killer T-like cells, IL-23⁺ natural killer cells, and IL-23-expressing macrophage populations (all P < 0.05). Regulatory T cells (Tregs) and CCR4⁺CCR6⁺ double-positive Tregs were also increased (P < 0.05). Plasma concentrations of IL-1β, tumour necrosis factor-α, IL-12p70, IL-17A, and IL-23 were significantly elevated in the scar group (all P < 0.05). Gene expression analysis identified persistent upregulation of nuclear factor kappa B1 (NFκB1; 2.21-fold) and IL-17 (3.38-fold). Paediatric burn survivors with hypertrophic scarring demonstrate persistent systemic immune dysregulation several years after injury. However, the cross-sectional design and absence of a normotrophic burn control group limit conclusions regarding whether these immune alterations are specific to pathological scarring or reflect broader long-term post-burn immune dysregulation.

articles.title: Marjolin ulcer: A single-center experience and evaluation of staging systems.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Marjolin ulcer lacks a disease-specific staging system, and existing cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) staging criteria have never been formally tested against outcomes in this disease. We retrospectively reviewed 42 consecutive Marjolin ulcer patients treated at a single tertiary center between 2010 and 2025, applied the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th edition and Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH) staging systems, and analyzed clinicopathological predictors of recurrence and survival including tumor depth of invasion (DOI) in millimeters. The cohort was predominantly male (71%) with a mean age of 54 years; burns were the leading etiology (67%), and the lower extremity was the most common site (69%). At median follow-up of 48 months, recurrence occurred in 26.2% and overall mortality in 21.4%. The AJCC system classified 71% of tumors as T3 and did not discriminate recurrence (p = 0.537) or mortality (p = 0.760). BWH staging was similarly nonsignificant. The AJCC cutaneous SCC depth threshold of 6 mm failed for recurrence (p = 0.477). When oral cavity SCC DOI thresholds were applied as an exploratory framework, patients with DOI ≤ 5 mm had no distant metastasis (0/23), whereas those with DOI > 10 mm had 80% recurrence and 60% distant metastasis (log-rank p < 0.001). Pathological nodal metastasis was the strongest independent predictor of recurrence-free survival (HR 5.91; p = 0.012). Current staging systems fail to stratify outcomes in Marjolin ulcer. Standardized reporting of DOI in millimeters alongside pathological nodal status across future series is needed for disease-specific staging and treatment algorithms.

articles.title: Secondary reconstruction of tendons and nerves improves long-term function in electrical burns of the wrist: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: High-voltage electrical burns can significantly damage the tendons and nerves, causing severe upper-limb dysfunction. Although early debridement and free flap coverage are proven techniques for limb salvage, the functional benefit of subsequent secondary tendon and nerve reconstruction has not been adequately investigated. Therefore, in this study, we assessed whether a systematic, staged reconstruction strategy improves long-term functional outcomes beyond those achieved with successful wound closure alone. A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted on 42 patients (all men) with type Ⅱ/Ⅲ electrical burns who were successfully treated with free flap coverage. The patients were stratified into a reconstruction group (n = 20) who received secondary tendon/nerve procedures and a non-reconstruction group (n = 22). The primary outcome was the QuickDASH score, evaluated at least 6 months postoperatively. The groups were compared after balancing for the baseline characteristics. The two groups were comparable in terms of age, injury severity, and initial flap outcomes. The reconstruction group underwent procedures such as tendon grafting (80%), tenolysis (80%), and nerve grafting (20%), at a mean of 6.15 months postinjury. Functional assessment revealed a significantly better (p < 0.001) median QuickDASH score in the reconstruction group (26.0) compared with that in the non-reconstruction group (39.5). Successful free flap coverage provides the key biological foundation for functional restoration. A systematic, staged protocol for tendon and nerve reconstruction considerably improves long-term limb function in patients with electrical burns of the wrist. Hence, secondary functional reconstruction is indispensable in the overall treatment plan for all eligible patients.

articles.title: Efficacy of fornix support ring in amniotic membrane transplantation for acute severe ocular burns.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the clinical efficacy and safety of amniotic membrane transplantation (AMT) enhanced with a fornix support ring for the treatment of severe acute ocular burns. Eighteen eyes of 15 patients with severe ocular burns (Grades III and IV) were included. Twelve eyes received AMT alone, while six eyes received AMT combined with a fornix support ring. Clinical outcomes, including best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure (IOP), and postoperative complications, were monitored over a follow-up period of 3-28 months. In the Grade III burn group, the addition of a fornix support ring to AMT significantly reduced the incidence of entropion and trichiasis compared to AMT alone (p = 0.018 for both). While the differences in symblepharon, keratitis, BCVA, and IOP changes did not reach statistical significance, clinical improvements were noted. Although statistical significance was not achieved in the Grade IV burn group, the group with the fornix support ring showed a reduced incidence of keratitis and other clinical differences. This study demonstrated that the fornix support ring is a reliable and effective option for enhancing surgical outcomes in acute ocular burns. By deepening the fornices, improving amniotic membrane adhesion, and reducing the need for extensive suturing, the ring significantly decreases the occurrence of complications, such as symblepharon, entropion, and trichiasis.

articles.title: PRDX4-enriched exosomes from adipose stem cells enhance diabetic wound repair through angiogenic activation.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Diabetic (DM) wounds are a major challenge in dermatology. Despite the therapeutic effectiveness of stem cell therapy in wound repair, clinical applications remain limited. We investigated whether adipose-derived exosomes (Exos) can promote healing in diabetic mice. High-throughput sequencing (HTS) was employed to study abnormal circular RNA expression in ulcerated tissue with or without adipose-derived stem cell (ADSC)-Exo treatment. EPCs were employed to analyze reactive oxygen species (ROS), apoptosis, and angiogenic differentiation functions. A DM ulceration mouse model was generated and Exo therapeutic effects were investigated. Data demonstrated that ADSC-Exo treatment enhances wound healing (WH) of diabetic mice through inhibiting ROS deposition and restoring angiogenic function under high glucose (HG) conditions. The HTS in the current research revealed that ADSC-Exo treatment resulted in altered gene expression, including of peroxiredoxin 4 (PRDX4). PRDX4 downregulation inhibited the Exo protective effects on WH. PRDX4 overexpression inhibited HG-induced EPC dysfunction and augmented Exo therapeutic effects on WH. Our data indicated that Exos derived from ADSCs promoted diabetic wound (DW) healing through delivering PRDX4 and improving endothelial cell function, which aids in the development of stem cell-based therapeutic treatments of DWs.

articles.title: Impact of hypothermia on the care outcome of burns patients transferred to a tertiary burn unit in NSW, Australia.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Hypothermia is common after major burn injury and may influence both systemic and wound-related outcomes. Although hypothermia has been associated with coagulopathy and higher rates of mortality in the trauma patient cohort, limited literature has examined its effects on the outcomes for patients with burns. The aim of this study was to identify the rate of hypothermia in patients transferred to a specialised burn unit, and to assess the impact on morbidity and mortality. This retrospective, single-centre study examined all burns presentations between 2009-2013. Hypothermia was defined as a core body temperature ≤ 35 °C on arrival. Statistical analysis used logistic regression for binary outcomes and negative binomial models for continuous outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression assessed hypothermia using continuous age, total body surface area burned (TBSA), and their interactions. Of 268 patients with recorded temperature, 41 (15%) were hypothermic. Hypothermia increased with burn size (11.6% in <20% TBSA vs 35.7% in >50% TBSA; p < 0.01). Hypothermic patients had higher mean age (46.6 vs 41.0 years; p < 0.05) and larger burns (22.8% vs 14.7% TBSA; p < 0.01). Adequate first aid and use of the modified Parkland Formula were less frequently documented in hypothermic patients (75.7% vs 92.3% and 60.7% vs 79.5%, respectively; both p < 0.01). There was no significant difference in burn size across age groups (p = 0.918). On multivariable analysis, increasing TBSA was independently associated with hypothermia, whereas age was not, and no significant age-TBSA interaction was identified (p = 0.647). Hypothermia was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (14.6% vs 3.5%), longer ICU LOS (4.39 vs 2.33 days), and higher sepsis rates (9.8% vs 2.6%); but lower rates of skin grafting (36.6% vs 51.1%) and shorter hospital LOS (17.3 vs 19.7 days). On multivariable analysis, hypothermia independently predicted mortality, LOS, grafting, wound infection and sepsis. Hypothermia remains common in burn patients transferred to a tertiary centre in NSW and is associated with larger burns, a higher average age, reduced adherence to early management protocols and poorer systemic outcomes despite reduced grafting rates and shorter hospital admissions.

articles.title: A 100-Day Workout Quality Improvement Project to Improve Value for the Care of Mental Health Conditions in a Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: The escalating mental health crisis among children has led to increased visits to the emergency department. Routine laboratory testing in children with behavioral and mental health (BMH) concerns is a common practice but rarely identifies clinically meaningful abnormalities. We aimed to reduce low-value care for patients requiring admission to our inpatient psychiatry unit by decreasing unnecessary testing and costs by 25%. We conducted a "100-day workout quality initiative" which used Lean Six Sigma methodology to implement an evidenced-based clinical pathway. After implementation, routine laboratory testing decreased from 96% to 20.8%. Overall costs associated with psychiatry admission in our institution decreased by 10%, with no adverse impact on clinical outcomes. This approach demonstrates a sustainable model for reducing low-value care in the emergency department setting for patients with BMH complaints.

articles.title: Unplanned Return Visits to the Emergency Department Following Circumferential Cast Applications for Pediatric Forearm Fractures.
articles.abstract: To quantify the incidence of and identify predictors for unplanned first-week return visits (1wRV) to the emergency department (ED) after circumferential casting (CC) application for pediatric forearm fractures. Retrospective, single-center study of patients aged 0 to 18 years with radius and/or ulna fractures. The primary outcome was unplanned ED revisit within 7 days (1wRV). Analyses included demographic variables, and fracture type, location, reduction versus casting in situ, and cast length. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify predictors of 1wRV. A total of 4661 cases were reviewed, with detailed analysis of 551 patients treated with CC in 2022. Among these, 67 (12.2%) experienced a 1wRV, most commonly due to pain (92.5%), with 95.5% requiring cast modification. Revisit rates varied by fracture location: distal radius and ulna (23.8%), midshaft radius and ulna (15.7%), distal radius (8.5%), and other fractures (5.5%; P =0.007), and were higher following reduction versus in-situ casting (16.1% vs. 4.3%; P <0.001; OR 3.265), peaking at 27.1% for reduced distal radius and ulna fractures. No compartment syndrome occurred, and 98.4% of patients completed nonoperative treatment successfully. Rates of 1wRV ranged from 0 to 27.1%, depending on fracture pattern and the need for reduction, and constituted the most common adverse event associated with CC. These granular findings underscore the need for a more individualized approach to immobilization and may inform the development of tailored, evidence-based nonoperative protocols for pediatric forearm fractures. Level.

articles.title: Air Transport Medicine: From the Field.
Maintaining Procedural Competence in Prehospital Emergency Anesthesia.
Just the facts: approach to the older patient with bilateral shoulder pain.
Frailty in Older Adults with Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) and frailty are increasingly prevalent with population aging, frequently coexist, and share pathophysiological mechanisms. This review summarizes recent evidence on shared biological pathways and management strategies in patients with HF and frailty. Emerging data suggest that accumulation of damaged cellular components, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and chronic inflammation contribute to both conditions. Altered myokine-mediated signaling further highlights skeletal muscle as an important peripheral link between HF and frailty and as a potential therapeutic target. Frailty is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant measure and potentially modifiable treatment target. Current evidence, largely derived from small or single-center studies, suggests that individualized multidomain interventions, including exercise training, nutritional optimization, and geriatric co-management, may improve patient-centered outcomes. Management should integrate guideline-directed HF therapy with targeted treatment of geriatric syndromes, guided by multidimensional assessment and individual patient goals. Multicenter trials in frail HF populations are needed to inform evidence-based management recommendations.

articles.title: inproTeamED - clinical reasoning in the emergency department as an individual and interprofessional process: a qualitative analysis.
articles.abstract: Patients in the emergency department (ED) are assessed and treated by the ED-Team consisting of nurses and physicians. The clinical assessment (CA) of emergency patients and the clinical reasoning (CR) of both professions play a decisive role in determining the quality of emergency care. This pilot study explores CR in daily routine practice of the ED on a cognitive-individual level, relying on the Dual-process Theory and on a social-interprofessional level, arguing interprofessional collaboration (IPC) as a part of CR. At least, organizational-structural factors influencing CR are analyzed as a third level. This is a qualitative study of 13 semi-structured individual interviews with nurses and physicians from three EDs in Germany, analysed using content analysis and methodological fundation. In the individual-cognitive CR, both physicians and nurses groups identified similar key factors for CA and used Systems 1 and 2 of the Dual-process Theory in their CR. On the social-interprofessional level, IPC was generally described positively, naming characteristics of good IPC and communication barriers were reported as rare. As possible organizational-structural factors influencing CR working experience as a prerequisite, size and region of the ED, age structure of the team and digitization were found. This pilot study provides insights into the CR of nurses and physicians in the ED and analyzes CR on an individual-cognitive, a social-interprofessional and an organizational-structural level, allowing to conclusions regarding the prerequisites for successful ED-teams.

articles.title: Integrating personal support workers to support older adults in the emergency department: a quantitative analysis.
articles.abstract: Our aim was to describe the pragmatic implementation of personal support workers in an ED setting, evaluating the characteristics of patients who were assigned to and received personal support worker care and the estimated operational impact of the program. This prospective observational cohort study was performed at a single ED during a pre (September 1/2022-February 28/2023) and post (March 11/2024-March 31/2025) intervention period. Requests were left to the discretion of any ED team member, including personal support workers. Using logistic regression, the primary outcome was patient characteristics. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital delirium rate, ED falls, ED length of stay using propensity score matching, and estimated redistribution of nursing hours with associated costs. There were 26,757 and 60,737 ED visits made during the control and intervention periods. In the latter group, 6,039 (9.9%) visits received personal support worker care. The three characteristics most strongly associated with care were age ≥ 65 years (OR: 7.1, p<0.001), ambulance arrival (OR: 3.9, p<0.001), and higher acuity triage score (OR: 3.3, p<0.001). After matching the 6,039 personal support worker-attended visits to (1) control period visits and (2) non-personal support worker-attended visits during the intervention period, the personal support worker-attended group was associated with an increased rate of in-hospital delirium (2.2%-2.5%, p<0.001) and ED length of stay (8.5-13.4 h, p<0.001) in both comparisons, and a trend toward increased ED falls in the second comparison (0.1%, p=0.06). In the personal support worker-attended group, an estimated 9 h of nursing time and $287.01Cdn in costs were redistributed per day. Left to the discretion of the ED staff, patients receiving personal support worker care were older, had longer ED length of stay and higher rate of in-hospital delirium. Personal support worker care was associated with an estimated redistribution of nursing hours, which could be redirected toward providing acute medical care.

articles.title: Confidence in the wild: the educational impact of a wilderness medicine workshop on emergency medicine resident self-confidence and perceptions.
articles.abstract: Wilderness medicine education has become an increasingly valued component of emergency medicine residency curricula but remains inconsistently integrated across programs. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a wilderness medicine educational workshop on residents' confidence in their provision of wilderness medicine care and their overall perception of wilderness medicine. A pre-test-post-test design was employed. The intervention of interest was an educational workshop composed of a lecture, rotating skills stations, and multiple simulated wilderness medicine scenarios. Data were collected through a survey completed prior to and immediately following the intervention. Twelve confidence and six perception competencies were assessed by the survey. A total of 22 participants comprised the study sample. Statistically significant differences were found post-intervention across wilderness medicine confidence outcomes as well as the confidence composite score (p < 0.001, r=0.905). All 12 competencies demonstrated moderate to large effect sizes (r > 0.50). Participants maintained favorable perceptions of wilderness medicine training across the workshop, with no significant post-intervention difference detected (p = 0.42). Our study highlights residents' favorable perceptions of wilderness medicine training and demonstrates the effectiveness of a single-day workshop in improving residents' confidence in wilderness medicine skills. This study supports the use of such interventions to further enhance medical residents' learning and self-reported confidence in important medical skills.

articles.title: Opioid-free analgesia for acute renal colic: a randomized, double-blind, head-to-head comparison of intravenous ibuprofen, dexketoprofen trometamol and paracetamol in the emergency department.
articles.abstract: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are first-line analgesics for acute renal colic, but comparisons of the intravenous (IV) non-opioid agents used in emergency departments are scarce. In this prospective, single-centre, randomized, double-blind, three-arm trial, 251 adults with acute renal colic received IV ibuprofen 400 mg (n = 86), dexketoprofen trometamol 50 mg (n = 82) or paracetamol 1 g (n = 83) infused over 15 min. Pain was scored on a 100-mm visual analogue scale (VAS) at 0, 15 and 30 min; the primary outcome was treatment success (≥50% VAS reduction at 30 min). Treatment success occurred in 76.7%, 74.4% and 66.3%, respectively (p = 0.280); mean VAS reduction at 30 min was 51.1, 56.5 and 45.5 mm. Baseline VAS was higher with dexketoprofen (85.2 vs 78.0 and 79.8 mm; p = 0.025); after adjustment for baseline, VAS at 30 min was lowest with dexketoprofen (25.6 mm), intermediate with ibuprofen (29.0 mm) and highest with paracetamol (35.1 mm; dexketoprofen vs paracetamol -9.5 mm, 95% confidence interval (CI) -16.5 to -2.5; p = 0.023). Rescue fentanyl was required in 32.6%, 31.7% and 43.4% (p = 0.217); the adjusted odds were lower with dexketoprofen than with paracetamol (odds ratio 0.40, 95% CI 0.20-0.84). Mild nausea or dizziness occurred in 3.5%, 3.7% and 3.6% of patients; none was serious. All three agents provided effective opioid-free analgesia; dexketoprofen produced the largest adjusted pain reduction and the lowest need for rescue opioid, ibuprofen was comparable and paracetamol least effective. Trial registration: not registered (see Methods).

articles.title: Rapid identification of severe hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia in hospitalized patients using laboratory-integrated machine learning.
articles.abstract: Dysglycemia is common in hospitalized patients and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Although central laboratory glucose testing is the diagnostic reference, clinically relevant delays may occur between sample processing and result reporting, particularly for critical values requiring urgent intervention. We investigated whether early photometric reaction signals generated during routine enzymatic glucose measurement could enable earlier recognition of severe dysglycemia.We developed a laboratory-based machine learning model to predict plasma glucose concentration using early analyzer-derived photometric absorbance features during the enzymatic reaction. Model development was performed, and performance was evaluated using an internal test split and an independent external validation cohort. Regression performance was assessed using mean absolute error, root mean squared error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination. Clinical risk classification was evaluated for severe dysglycemia defined as glucose <54 mg/dL or >250 mg/dL.In the internal test set, the model achieved high agreement between predicted and measured glucose concentrations (RMSE 7.1 mg/dL; R2 0.990). In external validation, prediction accuracy remained high (RMSE 45.1-52.0 mg/dL; R2 0.904-0.928 across evaluated models). For severe dysglycemia alerts (< 54 mg/dL or >250 mg/dL), multivariable linear regression provided the highest sensitivity (98.6%) with specificity of 90.9%..Analyzer-derived photometric reaction signals can be leveraged to predict glucose concentration and identify severe dysglycemia before routine test reporting is finalized. This laboratory-integrated approach may enhance patient safety by enabling earlier recognition of critical glucose abnormalities and supporting timely clinical decision-making. This approach may shorten the time to recognition of critical glucose abnormalities and facilitate earlier intervention.

articles.title: Prevalence of Persistent Severe Hypertension and Rates of Treatment Among Pregnant Patients in the Prehospital Setting.
articles.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) contribute to maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality and require time-sensitive intervention. In April 2025, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), in collaboration with the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) and the National Association of EMTs (NAEMT), published new guidelines on the prehospital management of elevated blood pressure in pregnancy. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent severe hypertension among pregnant patients encountered by prehospital clinicians, characterize baseline frequency of pre-guideline treatment, and establish a benchmark to inform implementation of these guidelines. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using the 2024 ESO Data Collaborative public release research dataset (January 1 to December 31, 2024). We identified all 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients documented as pregnant beyond 20 weeks of gestation. We excluded injury-related encounters and patients outside the World Health Organization-defined childbearing age range (15 to 49 years). Consistent with the new guidelines, we defined persistent severe hypertension as at least two documented blood pressure measurements with systolic blood pressure ≥ 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 110 mmHg. We defined guideline-adherent treatment as administration of both magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) and an antihypertensive medication (labetalol, hydralazine, or nifedipine). We identified 39,546 eligible 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients beyond 20 weeks of gestation. The prevalence of persistent severe hypertension was 3.1% (n = 1,234/39,546). Among these patients, 77 (6.2%) received magnesium sulfate only, 19 (1.5%) received an antihypertensive medication only, and 10 (0.8%) received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. Approximately 1 in 32 pregnant patients beyond 20 weeks of gestation encountered by prehospital clinicians had persistent severe hypertension. In the year prior to dissemination of the 2025 ACOG, NAEMSP, and NAEMT-supported guidelines, fewer than 1% received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. These findings establish a national benchmark and identify opportunities to improve prehospital care through protocol development, medication availability, clinician education, and implementation of updated guidelines.

articles.title: Field Medical Observations from a Remote High-Altitude Community on the Route to K2 (Askole Study I).
articles.abstract: BackgroundAskole (9843 ft [≈3000 m], Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan), the last village on the route to K2 Base Camp, is a remote high-altitude community with limited healthcare access, unsafe water, and infrastructural constraints. No systematic data describe its health burden, although such information is needed to plan future medical expeditions.MethodsFrom September 8 to 18, 2025 (11 working days), 2 Italian Alpine Club physicians provided medical care and health education at the Lorenzo Mazzoleni Dispensary. Clinical evaluation was supplemented by electrocardiography, ultrasonography, pulse oximetry, blood pressure measurement, and point-of-care glucometer and urine dipstick testing. School-based vision screening with the Lang stereotest was performed in Korphe.Results and DiscussionA total of 171 patients (174 visits; mean age 23.6 years) were evaluated. Gastrointestinal infectious diseases were most frequent, likely related to unsafe water and poor hygiene, followed by musculoskeletal disorders, chiefly lumbosacral radiculopathy, in adults. Skin, genitourinary, oral, ear, and ocular conditions were also common. Respiratory and cardiovascular symptoms occurred in relatively young individuals, without electrocardiographic evidence of ischemia, structural abnormality, or infarction; chronic mountain sickness was not systematically assessed. Vision screening identified stereoacuity deficits in 1.9% of children examined, all referred for ophthalmological evaluation. One new case of diabetes mellitus was diagnosed.ConclusionsInfectious disease is the main health burden in this setting. Improvements in water safety and infrastructure are essential, as health education alone is insufficient. These observations, limited by a small sample and short observation period, can nonetheless inform the planning of future medical expeditions.

Still's disease and malignancies: insights into the balance between inflammatory enhancement and immune control. Data from the International AIDA Network Still's Disease Registry.
authors: From the International AIDA (AutoInflammatory Diseases Alliance) Network, from the Autoinflammatory Diseases Working Group of the Italian Society of Rheumatology (SIR)
articles.abstract: Still's disease is an autoinflammatory condition marked by excessive activation of the innate immune system, resulting in intense and persistent systemic inflammation if left untreated. Chronic inflammation is recognized as both an initiator and promoter of carcinogenesis, although growing evidence suggests it may act against cancer development. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the cancer risk in patients with Still's disease. Data were obtained from the international Autoinflammatory Diseases Alliance (AIDA) Network registry for Still's disease. Statistical analysis included a machine learning-based approach to evaluate associations between independent variables and malignancy. A total of 626 patients with Still's disease were included, of whom 14 (2.2%) developed 15 malignant neoplasms. Patients with malignancy history exhibited higher age at disease onset and diagnosis, as well as longer duration of fever during flares. Machine learning-based analysis, including Elastic Net and Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression, identified an association between cancer development and fever duration (relative risk = 1.002, 95% confidence interval 1.000-1.004, p = 0.01). Despite being a severe systemic inflammatory condition, Still's disease appears to be associated with a relatively modest prevalence of cancer. However, uncontrolled systemic inflammation, as reflected by prolonged fever duration, may contribute to carcinogenesis in these patients.

articles.title: Impact of pre-existing bleeding disorders on outcomes in patients with traumatic brain injury.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major global public health problem. This study aimed to evaluate the association between pre-existing bleeding disorders and clinical outcomes among patients with TBI. We hypothesized that pre-existing bleeding disorders would be associated with worse outcomes following TBI. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2021-2023 National Inpatient Sample (NIS) to evaluate the association between pre-existing bleeding disorders and clinical outcomes among patients aged 15 years or older hospitalized with TBI. Mortality was significantly higher in the bleeding disorder group (13.9% vs. 4.8%; p < 0.001), the median length of stay was longer (5 days vs. 3 days; p < 0.001), median hospitalization costs were substantially higher (US $20,582 vs. US $13,515; p < 0.001), and discharge home was less frequent (44.8% vs. 61.6%; p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, comorbidity burden, injury severity, and other clinically relevant covariates, pre-existing bleeding disorders remained independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.99-2.69). Pre-existing bleeding disorders were independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality after TBI. Patients with these disorders also experienced worse clinical outcomes. Early recognition and appropriate hemostatic assessment may support individualized management in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: 24-hour risk updating for major ICU complications after severe trauma: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Conventional trauma prognostic models rely primarily on admission data and cannot account for subsequent physiological response to treatment. We evaluated whether routinely collected physiological information available at 24 h provides incremental prognostic information for major intensive care unit (ICU) complications in severely injured patients. We conducted a prospective cohort of adults with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score [ISS] ≥ 15) admitted to the ICU between January 2024 and April 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of major respiratory, hemodynamic, renal, or septic complications during the ICU course. TRISS was compared with an admission ridge model incorporating ISS, Glasgow Coma Scale, hemoglobin, lactate, and international normalized ratio, and a 24-h updated ridge model additionally incorporating 24-h lactate and change in creatinine. Performance was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Among 109 patients, median ISS was 29 (IQR 20-38), and 73 (67.0%) developed major ICU complications. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 for TRISS, 0.873 for the admission model, and 0.887 for the 24-h updated model; Brier scores were 0.178, 0.140, and 0.131. Compared with the admission model, the 24-h updated model improved performance (ΔAUC 0.016, 95% bootstrap interval 0.004-0.030; ΔBrier - 0.010, - 0.017 to - 0.005). Twenty-four-hour lactate and creatinine change were the strongest contributors to the update. In severely injured ICU patients, incorporating physiological evolution during the first 24 h refined admission-based prognostic assessment. Lactate and creatinine trajectories provided incremental information for major ICU complications during the ICU course. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Comparing Autologous Skin Grafting vs. Cultured Epithelial Autografts in Severe Burn Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Wound Healing and Scarring.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: This randomized controlled trial compared autologous skin grafting (ASG) and cultured epithelial autografts (CEA) in patients with severe burns. A total of 120 patients with burns involving more than 30% of the total body surface area were randomly assigned to ASG (n = 60) or CEA (n = 60). Primary outcomes included wound healing time, 2-week graft survival, and Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS) scores at 3 and 6 months. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, complications, and serum biomarkers. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Compared with ASG, CEA was associated with a longer wound healing time and lower 2-week graft survival. However, VSS scores at both follow-up time points were significantly lower in the CEA group. Postoperative pain at 72 hours and complication rates were also lower in patients treated with CEA. In addition, epidermal growth factor and transforming growth factor-β1 levels were higher, while C-reactive protein levels were lower in the CEA group at 3 days postoperatively. In conclusion, although CEA results in delayed wound healing, it offers improved scar quality, reduced pain, and fewer complications, and may serve as an effective alternative for severe burn patients with limited donor skin.

articles.title: Prehospital Care of Older Adults Following Perceived Low-Acuity Falls and Related "Lift Assist" Encounters: An NAEMSP Position Statement and Resource Document.
articles.abstract: Older adults who present as low-acuity falls requiring mobilization assistance, commonly referred to as a "lift assist", represent a common reason for EMS activation. These encounters often involve underlying medical conditions or injuries that are not immediately apparent, and missed or delayed diagnosis is associated with adverse outcomes. At the same time, some patients are transported to the emergency department when it is not necessary, exposing them to potential harms and contributing to increased health care utilization. These encounters are therefore complex clinical presentations and represent important opportunities for thorough assessment and higher-order clinical decision making, supported by systems that enable appropriate disposition and follow-up. However, there is a system-level bias, beginning in initial education and reinforced through dispatch, policy, and protocol, that frames these encounters as uniformly low-acuity, non-medical, minor traumas leading to underassessment and limiting clinical decision-making. Therefore, NAEMSP recommends:EMS systems should recognize calls for falls or "lift assists" as patient encounters that warrant an assessment, including evaluation for underlying medical causes, traumatic injuries, and safety, and frame these encounters as opportunities for higher-order clinical decision-making within the broader context of geriatric syndromes rather than isolated low-acuity events.EMS systems should support transport decisions based on a thorough assessment and patient-centered discussion, recognizing that not all patients require ED transport and that safe alternatives may include non-transport or referral to appropriate follow-up pathways.EMS systems should track the assessment of patients encountered during "lift assist" responses and older adults following perceived low acuity falls as a system-level quality measure to monitor performance and drive improvement.Policymakers and payers should implement sustainable reimbursement structures that support EMS assessment and care even when transport does not occur.

articles.title: Implementing a Physician Annual Unpaid Sabbatical for Escape: utilizing a rotating "PAUSE" month to improve wellness amongst emergency medicine physicians.
Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.
articles.abstract: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor regarding "The fracture orthopedic risk of non-home discharge (FORD) score: A novel bedside predictive tool for non-home discharge in orthopedic trauma patients".
Union rate and time to union following platelet-rich plasma therapy in fracture nonunion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Fracture nonunion remains a challenging clinical problem associated with prolonged disability and repeated surgical interventions. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been proposed as a biological adjunct to enhance bone healing; however, clinical evidence remains inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of PRP in the management of fracture nonunion. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO Registration: CRD420261366849). PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies evaluating PRP in fracture nonunion and reporting union rate or time to union were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to compare PRP with control interventions. Risk ratios (RR) were calculated for union rates and standardized mean differences (SMD) for time to union. Additional single-arm analyses were performed to estimate pooled outcomes in PRP-treated cohorts. Twenty-one studies comprising 877 patients were included. Two comparative studies (n = 119) demonstrated a higher likelihood of union with PRP (RR 1.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.36, p < 0.05) without significant heterogeneity. Six studies (n = 250) showed no significant difference in time to union between PRP and control groups (SMD -0.72, 95% CI -1.48-0.05), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 85%). In PRP-only analyses, the pooled union rate was 0.86 (95% CI 0.76-0.94; I² = 61%) across seven studies (n = 150), and the pooled mean time to union was 6.08 months (95% CI 4.26-7.90; I² = 100%) across eight studies (n = 187). PRP was associated with higher union rates in the limited comparative evidence, although no statistically significant difference in time to union was demonstrated. Heterogeneity in PRP protocols, methodological limitations, and the small comparative evidence base limit the certainty of these findings. PRP may have a potential role as a biological adjunct in fracture nonunion management, but further well-designed randomized controlled trials are required before definitive clinical recommendations can be made.

articles.title: Patients experiencing homelessness in an urban emergency department: experience from a tertiary center in Tel Aviv.
articles.abstract: People experiencing homelessness represent a distinct emergency department (ED) population, often lacking regular medical follow-up and experiencing delays in necessary care. ED visits commonly relate to unmet basic needs, chronic medical conditions, psychiatric illness, or substance-related complications. In many healthcare systems, unhoused populations are described as "super users" of emergency services. However, data on homelessness and ED utilization in Israel are limited. We conducted a historical cohort study at the Emergency Department of Tel Aviv Medical Center. ED visits between January 7, 2022 and May 31, 2023 involving patients documented as unhoused were identified using systematic free-text keyword searches. The demographics, presenting complaints, investigations, interventions, and dispositions were extracted. A longitudinal database (2018-2023) was constructed for each individual, capturing chronic illness, psychiatric diagnoses, substance use, repeat ED visits, hospitalizations, and outpatient utilization. Analyses were descriptive. Of 214 identified ED visits 149 persons experiencing homelessness were included. Most patients were men (84%), with a median age of 43 years, and 92% were living on the street. Available records suggested prolonged homelessness, though documentation was incomplete. High rates of chronic disease, infectious conditions, psychiatric disorders, and substance or alcohol use were observed. Most individuals presented once or only a few times; however, a small subgroup demonstrated frequent ED utilization, including some with more than 30 visits over 5 years. Common presentations included psychiatric complaints, trauma, substance-related conditions, and nonspecific pain. Only 1% of visits resulted in hospitalization. In this urban ED, homelessness was not uniformly associated with frequent emergency care use; rather, high utilization was concentrated in a small subset of patients. The substantial burden of psychiatric illness, substance use, chronic disease, and infection highlights complex medical and social needs. ED encounters represent opportunities for targeted interventions, harm-reduction strategies, and improved linkage to community and municipal services.
